background.summary: However, two critical issues remain underexplored: 1) severe foreground-background imbalance caused by large scene coverage hinders reliable object recognition; 2) aerial objects exhibit substantial local variations in scale, orientation, and structure, which hinder accurate localization.

evidence.quote: However, two critical issues remain underexplored: 1) severe foreground-background imbalance caused by large scene coverage hinders reliable object recognition; 2) aerial objects exhibit substantial local variations in scale, orientation, and structure, which hinder accurate localization.

I NTRODUCTION ERIAL object detection is a fundamental task in remote sensing, with applications in urban management, traffic surveillance, maritime monitoring, and disaster response.

Most existing methods rely on RGB inputs, whose limited spectral representation often struggles under illumination changes, occlusions, and background interference, especially when objects resemble surrounding regions.
